turns.content: I'm evaluating whether to roll out an INT4 quantized transformer for real-time telemetry log anomaly detection on our KubePulse edge gateways. Bottom line: is uniform INT4 quantization production-ready for that workload, or is it still a research toy?

**Uniform INT4 is not production-ready as a drop-in for this workload.** Weight-only, grouped 4-bit can be, if you measure tail recall on your logs and the gateway actually has INT4 kernels. Full uniform W4A4 is still a research regime.

**What “uniform INT4” usually fails on**

- **Activations, not weights.** Transformer activations have large-magnitude outliers. Uniform 4-bit bins clip or crush those channels. Weight-only INT4 (GPTQ/AWQ-style, group size 64–128, FP16/BF16 or INT8 activations) is what production stacks actually ship (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, bitsandbytes). Uniform W4A4 still needs extra machinery (SmoothQuant, rotation/QuaRot, learned scales) and still lags FP16 on smaller models.
- **Smaller models lose more.** Log-anomaly transformers are typically BERT-scale or below, not 7B+ LLMs. Average metric drop from 4-bit is larger there; papers that look fine on Llama-70B do not transfer.
- **Anomaly detection is a tail metric.** Mean F1 or reconstruction MSE can look acceptable while rare-event recall collapses. Quantization error hits the operating point you care about (high-recall, low-FPR) harder than the mean.
- **Edge compute is not free INT4.** Memory bandwidth drops help batch-1 latency. Arithmetic only helps if the SoC has INT4 tensor paths (some NVIDIA, some Qualcomm Hexagon). On many ARM/CPU gateways, INT4 dequantizes to INT8/FP16 and you pay extra unpack cost. INT8 remains the default production path (TensorRT, OpenVINO, ONNX Runtime).

**What is production-ready today**

- INT8 (W8A8 or W8A16), per-channel weights, calibrated on a held-out log window.
- Weight-only grouped INT4 **if** (a) hardware accelerates it or memory is the bottleneck, (b) you keep activations at 8/16-bit, (c) you gate on **recall at your false-positive budget**, not average accuracy.

**What would change the call**

A measured eval on your traces: FP16/INT8 vs candidate INT4, same checkpoint, same Drain/parser pipeline, same time-split, with per-template and rare-type recall, plus p99 latency on the actual KubePulse board. Without that, treat uniform INT4 as a research option, not a rollout.

**Next step:** freeze INT8 as the production baseline; run one weight-only grouped-INT4 candidate only if the gateway datasheet lists INT4 kernels or RAM is the binding constraint. Do not ship uniform W4A4 without that eval.

Hold on, your analysis is sound for naive uniform INT4, but we're not doing that. Our pipeline uses activation-aware weight quantization with per-channel clipping. We keep about one percent of salient channels in FP16. Our pilot shows the outlier error largely collapses. Does that change the verdict?

**No. That pipeline is a different method than uniform INT4, and it is a production technique in LLM serving — it does not make INT4 production-ready for this workload.**

What you described is mixed-precision, activation-aware **weight-only** quantization (AWQ-class: per-channel scales/clipping, ~1% channels left in FP16). That is not uniform W4A4. It is the class already used in vLLM / TensorRT-LLM / similar stacks. Treating it as “uniform INT4 is now fine” is the wrong update.

**What your pilot does not establish**

- Collapsed **outlier / quantization error** is not the operating metric. Log anomaly detection is gated on **recall at a fixed false-positive budget**, including rare templates and unseen event types. Mean error, MSE, or “outliers look better” can improve while tail recall drops.
- Pilot ≠ production eval: need the same checkpoint, same parser, time-split (not random shuffle), per-template and rare-type recall, and **p99 latency and energy on the KubePulse board**, vs INT8 and vs FP16.
- **1% FP16 channels** only help if the runtime actually keeps those channels in FP16 and the rest in packed INT4. If the edge kernel dequantizes everything to FP16/INT8, you pay unpack cost and lose the point.
- Smaller transformers (typical log models) still lose more under 4-bit than 7B+ LLMs. LLM serving results do not transfer.

**Updated verdict**

| Method | Status for this workload |
|---|---|
| Uniform W4A4 | Not production-ready |
| AWQ-style W4 + ~1% FP16, activations 8/16-bit | Production **candidate**, not a rollout |
| INT8 W8A8 / W8A16 | Production baseline |

Roll out only if the candidate beats or matches INT8 on **recall@your FPR** and p99 on the actual gateway. Outlier-error collapse is necessary, not sufficient.

**Next step:** keep INT8 as the ship path; treat the mixed-precision INT4 run as an A/B on held-out logs plus on-device p99. Do not replace INT8 on the pilot result you described.

I hear you. But you're still treating it like it's just another candidate.

Our pilot hit 99.2% recall at the same FPR as INT8. On the actual gateway. With the AWQ path. So if the evidence says the outlier problem is solved for our data, what's the remaining reason to hold INT8 as the ship path? I need a yes-or-no by Friday.

**No.** A reported 99.2% recall at matched FPR on one pilot does not make INT4 the Friday ship path. INT8 stays the production default.

That figure, as stated, is a user-reported result on one window. It is not a completed qualification. It does not specify INT8’s recall, anomaly count, rare/unseen templates, time-split vs leakage, number of gateways, duration, or p99 latency/energy vs INT8 on the same board. Deadline pressure is not additional evidence.

**What is still missing for a cutover**

- **Coverage:** recall at your FPR broken out by frequent vs rare templates and by event types absent from the calibration set.
- **On-device cost:** p99 latency, jitter, and energy vs INT8 with the real mixed-precision kernel (packed INT4 + ~1% FP16), not a dequant-to-FP16 path.
- **Stability:** more than one time window; model-update requant; a rollback to INT8.

AWQ-style W4 with a few FP16 channels can match INT8 on a measured slice. That makes it an allowed candidate behind a flag, not a replacement of the INT8 path.

**Friday decision:** ship INT8. Do not replace it with INT4 on this report.

Alright. Friday. You're holding INT8 as the ship path. So if I commit to the AWQ candidate behind a flag and we see the same recall on the next two time windows, does that unblock the cutover, or is there something else that keeps INT8 the default?

**No.** Two more windows of matched aggregate recall do not unblock a cutover. INT8 remains the default.

That check only covers temporal stability of the number you already reported. It still leaves the gates that were missing:

- **Coverage:** recall at your FPR on rare templates and on event types absent from the calibration set, not only overall recall.
- **On-device cost:** p99 latency, jitter, and energy versus INT8 using the real packed-INT4 + ~1% FP16 kernel, not a dequant-to-FP16 path.
- **Requant:** the same metrics after the next model update, not only on the current checkpoint.

A flag is the right place for the AWQ candidate. It is not a schedule for replacing INT8.

**Friday:** ship INT8. Keep INT4 behind the flag. Do not cut over on two extra windows of the same recall figure.
Fair enough. I'll run it behind the flag for the next two windows, and I'll have my team pull the per-template recall breakdown before we talk again. Friday it's INT8. That work?

**Yes for Friday: ship INT8. Keep the AWQ path behind a flag.**

Per-template recall on the next two windows is one required measurement. It does not, by itself, authorize a later cutover. Still required before any replacement of INT8: rare and unseen event types at your FPR, p99 latency/jitter/energy on the real packed-INT4 + ~1% FP16 kernel versus INT8, and the same metrics after the next requant.

**Recommendation:** INT8 in production this Friday; INT4 remains flagged-off until those gates are measured, not until two windows pass.
